results.title: How do you tune similarity thresholds for better relevance?
results.content: Tuning similarity thresholds involves adjusting the cutoff value that determines whether two items (e.g., search results, user profiles, or documents) are considered relevant matches. Start by evaluating your system’s performance using metrics like precision, recall, or F1-score across different threshold values. For example, if your search engine returns too many irrelevant results (low precision), raising the threshold might filter out weaker matches. Use A/B testing to compare user engagement (e.g., click-through rates, time spent) between different thresholds. If users consistently ignore low-relevance results, it signals the threshold is too low. For example, a system could use a lower threshold for rare search terms where fewer results exist. Implement feedback loops that log user interactions (e.g., skipped results, repeated searches) to retrain models or adjust thresholds periodically. For semantic search systems using embeddings, calculate similarity scores (e.g., cosine similarity) across a sample dataset and set thresholds based on score distributions. Tools like grid search or Bayesian optimization can systematically explore thresholds.
